aliasNameHelp: The sender’s identifiers are stored on devices as the alias “custom.<name>”. Lower-case letters, digits, hyphen and underscore.
aliasNameInvalid: Use lower-case letters, digits, hyphen or underscore, up to 63 characters.
authFailureHint: A request for this integration has failed authentication. Check the token the sender presents.
clearConfirm: Forget everything listed here? These are observations only; one the sender is still sending is listed again.
connectDescription: What to enter in the sender. The bearer token is shown once, when it is generated or rotated, and cannot be shown again.
copyManually: Copying was not possible here. Select the field and copy it by hand.
createDeviceWithAlias: Create a device with this alias
deleteConfirm: Delete integration “{{token}}”? The sender is refused at once. Aliases on devices are kept. This cannot be undone.
enabledHelp: Turn off to stop resolving devices through this integration at once.
frameEncodingHelp: How the frame is written in the body.
framePointerHelp: A JSON pointer to an encoded raw frame, kept for a decoder. The frame is not decoded yet.
framePointerInvalid: This is not a JSON pointer, or the encoding is set without one.
healthDescription: What this integration has received and could not use.
healthUndecodedNote: An uplink counts here when it carries no decoded object with a numeric value. For a network server, set a codec on the device profile there and use JSON encoding.
idKindHelp_binary: A binary body has no fields, so the identifier is a request header or a query parameter.
idKindHelp_json: A field of the JSON body, a request header, or a query parameter.
idValueHelp_header: The header name, such as X-Device-Id.
idValueHelp_pointer: A JSON pointer to the field, such as /device/id.
idValueHelp_query: The query parameter name, such as device.
idValueInvalid: This is not a valid location for that kind (a JSON pointer starts with “/”).
identityHelp: How the sender names a device: by its DevEUI, or by its device id in the network server.
itemsPointerHelp: A JSON pointer to an array in the body; each element is one uplink. Leave empty when the body is a single uplink.
itemsPointerInvalid: This is not a JSON pointer (it starts with “/”).
linkMetricsHelp: Signal strength, signal-to-noise ratio and gateway count are stored beside each decoded uplink.
listDescription: Authenticated senders of device data over HTTP, such as a LoRaWAN network server or a webhook
listEmpty: No integrations yet. Create one to let a network server or a webhook send device data to this tenant.
revealCreatedBody: This is the bearer token for “{{token}}”. Enter it in the sender now.
revealRotatedBody: This is the new bearer token for “{{token}}”. The previous one no longer works.
revealShownOnce: Copy it now. It is shown only once and cannot be read again; if it is lost, rotate it.
rotateConfirm: Replace the bearer token of “{{token}}”? The old token stops working at once, with no overlap, so update the sender straight after. The new one is shown once.
scopeHelp: Only devices of these types are resolved through this integration, whatever the sender claims. At least one.
scopeRequired: Choose at least one device type.
snippetChirpstackCodec: Set a codec on the ChirpStack device profile. Without one an uplink carries no decoded values and is counted as undecoded here.
snippetChirpstackIntro: In ChirpStack, open the application, add an HTTP integration, and fill it in as follows.
snippetChirpstackJson: Encoding must be JSON. A Protobuf integration is refused with a message naming the setting.
snippetChirpstackQuery: ChirpStack adds the event type to the URL itself; only uplinks are read and other events are acknowledged and ignored.
snippetGenericIntro: Send each uplink as an HTTP POST. For example:
snippetGenericRetries: Without a sender time configured, a retried request is stored twice.
snippetTtsCodec: Set a payload formatter on the application or device in The Things Stack. Without one an uplink carries no decoded values and is counted as undecoded here.
snippetTtsIntro: In The Things Stack, add a custom webhook to the application and fill it in as follows.
snippetTtsOthers: Messages on any other path are acknowledged and ignored.
snippetTtsPaths: Enable the uplink message on one of these paths: {{paths}}.
timePointerHelp: A JSON pointer to the time the sender recorded. Without it the time of receipt is used, and a retried request is stored twice.
timePointerInvalid: This is not a JSON pointer (it starts with “/”).
title: Integrations
tokenFixed: The token is part of the sender’s URL and cannot be changed.
tokenHelp: Part of the URL the sender posts to. The bearer token it authenticates with is generated for you.
typeFixed: The type cannot be changed after the integration is created.
typeHelp_CHIRPSTACK_V4: A ChirpStack v4 server with its HTTP integration. Uplinks must be sent as JSON.
typeHelp_GENERIC_BINARY: Any sender of raw binary bodies. The device identifier comes from a header or a query value. The frame is counted but not decoded yet.
typeHelp_GENERIC_JSON: Any sender of JSON bodies. You say where the device identifier is.
typeHelp_TTS_V3: A The Things Stack v3 webhook.
undecodedHint: Uplinks arrived with nothing to read readings from. Check the codec in the network server.
unregisteredDescription: Identifiers this integration received that no device in its scope carries. Create a device with the alias to start storing its data.
unregisteredEmpty: None seen. Identifiers the sender uses that no device carries will appear here.
